keyframe_review.note: 4,857 km2 for 1709-1712 (64.7-65.7 E, 30.8-31.6 N): the Kandahar oasis. The Hotak page: 'Hotak revolt: 21 April 1709', the Georgian garrison expelled; the Mirwais page: Hotak 'declared independence of the Loy Kandahar region' and beat the Persian force of 1710 and four more armies in 18 months. The pages give no area.

149,398 km2 for 1713-1717 (60.9-66.4 E, 30.4-35.3 N): the province of Kandahar with the Helmand. The Hotak page: after the Persian commander died near Herat in 1712 Mirwais 'was able to extend his control over the entire province of Kandahar'. The date is a year earlier than Cliopatria's; Zamindawar, Farah and the north edge are on neither page (the Mirwais page puts a Persian governor at Farah).

552,632 km2 for 1718-1720 (58.9-66.7 E, 25.0-35.3 N): adds Sistan and Balochistan to the Makran coast. Unverified: the Mahmud page has only the campaign of 1720 ('crossed the deserts of Sistan and captured Kerman'; the siege of Kerman began that year) and a victory over the Sadozai Sultanate of Herat that year, and the Mirwais page is silent on Quetta and Baluchistan. The year 1718 is Cliopatria's.

correction.text: unchanged shape, year 1721 only; 1722-1726 see the new keyframe hotaki-dynasty_1722

keyframe_review.note: 919,074 km2 for 1721-1726 (56.0-66.7 E, 25.0-37.5 N): Kandahar, Sistan, Balochistan and 187 cells of Kerman province east of the town (29.1-31.9 N, 56.5-59.5 E; the town of Kerman, 57.08 E 30.30 N, lies outside the shape, as the Mahmud page has it: 'easily conquered the Kirman town but failed to take its citadel' in October 1721, and the city was never captured; fx-49 deleted the ledger gain of the whole province). It lacks Isfahan: the Afghans routed the Persian army at Gulnabad on 8 March 1722, besieged Isfahan and Shah Soltan Hoseyn handed over the crown on 23 October 1722; Mahmud then took Shiraz, Golpayegan and Kashan (1722-1723). Cliopatria first draws Isfahan in 1727. [fx-14 2026-11-01: from/to 1721 added, as the correction text says 'year 1721 only'; without them data/shapes.csv ran the shape to 1726 beside hotaki-dynasty_1722, which contains it.]

correction.text: the Kandahar-Sistan-Kerman lands of 1721 with Isfahan, Shiraz and Kashan, the central Persia of Mahmud and Ashraf

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1722-1726: the 1721 shape plus Isfahan, Shiraz and Kashan. Qazvin was taken 'but the population revolted in January 1723', and the Ottomans and Russians seized Persian land 'during the chaos, reducing Mahmud's territory' (undated). The Kuhgelu tribesmen defeated an army south of Isfahan and Yazd was not taken.

correction.text: unchanged shape, years 1727-1729 only; from 1730 the Kandahar outline (hotaki-dynasty_1730)

keyframe_review.note: 1,918,357 km2 for 1727-1733 (47.7-66.7 E, 25.0-38.5 N): the Afghan empire at its largest, with Isfahan, Fars, Kerman and the west to Hamadan. Right for 1727-1729 as the best outline of 'most of Iran' (Mahmud page): the Ottoman agreement of October 1727 'let the Ottomans keep the Iranian lands they occupied' (so the west edge is soft) and Ashraf signed with Russia at Rasht in February 1729. He 'fled Isfahan on 13 November 1729, three days before Nader entered the city', and killed in early 1730; 'After 1729, Hotak rule was limited to the south of Afghanistan'. Cliopatria keeps the Persian lands to 1733. [fx-14 2026-11-01: from/to 1727-1729 added, as the correction text says. Without them data/shapes.csv ran this shape to 1733, so at 1730 the compiler drew the union of this outline and hotaki-dynasty_1730 (7,357 cells, the Persian lands back) and at 1734 snapped 5,208 cells off again. Hotak dynasty page (opened 2026-11-01): '1729: Ashraf Hotak was banished to what is now southern Afghanistan, limiting Hotak rule to a vestige of their once large empire'.]

correction.text: the southern Afghan lands of Hussain Hotak (Kandahar), 552,475 km2

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1730-1733: the Kandahar-Sistan outline of Cliopatria's 1734 shape, applied from the loss of Persia ('Hotak rule was limited to the south of Afghanistan' after 1729; Nader 'drove out the remaining Ghilji forces from Persia').

552,475 km2 for 1734-1737 (58.9-66.7 E, 25.0-35.3 N): the same outline as 1718-1720. The Hussain page: 'Kandahar remained under Hussain's control until 1738' and names no other territory, so the Sistan and Balochistan parts are unverified: page silent. Nader took Kandahar in 1738 (24 March on the Hotak page's infobox); Cliopatria ends the row in 1737, a year early.

correction.text: the Kandahar lands of Hussain Hotak, to March 1738

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1738: the 1734 outline in the last year, to the fall of Kandahar on 24 March 1738 ('Nader Shah's forces went on to conquer Kandahar in 1738').

region.text: Kandahar and the Loy Kandahar region

ledger.note: 21 April 1709: Mirwais Hotak rises at Kandahar. Infobox 'Hotak revolt: 21 April 1709'; Mirwais 'ambushed Gurgin Khan on 21 April and killed him' and the Georgian garrison was expelled; he 'declared independence of the Loy Kandahar region' (Mirwais page).

1710: the first Persian army is beaten. 'In 1710, the Persians dispatched a force under Muhammad Khan' and Hotak defeated it; 'Over 18 months, the Persians dispatched four more armies, but each was defeated.'

1712: the Persian effort ends. After the commander of the 1712 Persian army died in Herat (Zaman Khan, spring 1712 on the Mirwais page) Mirwais 'was able to extend his control over the entire province of Kandahar'.

region.text: the province of Kandahar round the oasis, 149,000 km2 in Cliopatria's 1713 shape

ledger.note: 1712: Mirwais holds the whole province of Kandahar. 'After the 1712 Persian army's commander died in Herat, Mirwais was able to extend his control over the entire province of Kandahar.' Cliopatria draws the larger shape from 1713. Zamindawar, Farah and Herat are not placed by the pages.

region.text: Sistan, Balochistan and the Makran coast added in Cliopatria's 1718 shape (about 400,000 km2)

ledger.note: 1718: Sistan and Balochistan join the Hotak shape. A bridging event: the date is Cliopatria's; the Mahmud page has only the campaign of 1720 across Sistan, and the Mirwais page is silent on Baluchistan. The former owner is read as the Safavid provinces of Sistan, with Baloch lands.

1720: Mahmud besieges Kerman. 'He began his first campaign by besieging Kerman' and defeated the Sadozai Sultanate of Herat in battle that year; Hotak page: his forces 'crossed the deserts of Sistan and captured Kerman'.

October 1721: the last dated action at Kerman. 'The Ghilzais easily conquered the Kirman town but failed to take its citadel on October 1721' and lost 'one thousand five hundred men' (Mahmud page); in 1722 he 'encountered Kirman yet again at the unwelcoming sight of re-inforced defenses outside the city', 'failed to capture it' and 'bypassed it'. The contest closes here with no change of owner: Kerman stays Safavid. Fix fx-49 (2 Nov 2026, request R088 of window p1720-p1729): the former ledger/7, a gain of the whole Kerman province in October 1721, was deleted as the page contradicts it; the note used to read 'Kerman falls'. (The Hotak dynasty page's 'crossed the deserts of Sistan and captured Kerman' is the other reading; the Mahmud page, which gives the dated detail, is followed.)
October 1722: the court moves to Isfahan (infobox 'Isfahan (1722-1729)'); Kandahar stays Hussain's seat.
8 March 1722: the Safavid army is routed at Gulnabad. 'At the Battle of Gulnabad, the Afghans routed the Persian army and advanced on Isfahan.' The siege began with the capture of Julfa.

23 October 1722: Isfahan surrenders. 'The siege ended on 23 October 1722'; Shah Soltan Hoseyn placed his crown on Mahmud's turban at Farahabad (Hotak page: he 'acknowledged Mahmud as the new Shah of Persia').
23 October 1722: Mahmud becomes shah at Isfahan. The siege of about six months ended with the abdication; Mahmud 'then reigned as shah'; infobox 'Isfahan (1722-1729)'.

region.text: Shiraz (Fars), Kashan and Golpayegan taken by Mahmud

ledger.note: 1722-1723: Shiraz, Golpayegan and Kashan fall to Mahmud (undated on the page; 1723 is the later year). Qazvin was taken in November 1722 but 'the population revolted in January 1723'. Confidence 1 (reviewer ia-03-d, 2026-10-19): the Mahmud page gives no year for Shiraz, Golpayegan or Kashan, so the year is a bridging judgment.

region.text: the Ottoman-Afghan front in western Persia: Khorramabad and Kermanshah

ledger.note: November 1726: the Ottoman and Afghan armies meet at Khorramabad. 'The Ottomans ordered a campaign in spring 1726. The armies met at Khorramabad in November 1726, and the Afghans won.' (The lead says near Kermanshah.) Earlier, 'The Ottomans and Russians seized Persian land during the chaos' (Mahmud page, undated).

region.text: the western Persian lands the Ottomans kept

ledger.note: October 1727: the Ottoman peace. The agreement 'was not ratified' but 'let the Ottomans keep the Iranian lands they occupied while recognizing Ashraf's rule'. The page names no treaty or town; the usual 'Treaty of Hamadan' is not on it.

region.text: central Persia between Damghan, Tehran and Isfahan

ledger.note: 29 September 1729: Nader beats the Afghans at Mehmandust. 'Nader defeated an Afghan force at Mehmandust near Damghan on 29 September 1729' and 'pushed Ashraf back from Tehran to Isfahan' (Hotak page: Ashraf's defeat at Damghan in the infobox 29 September 1729).
13 November 1729: Ashraf flees Isfahan. He 'fled Isfahan on 13 November 1729, three days before Nader entered the city'; Nader beat him at Zarghan and Pol-e Fasa (no dates).

region.text: Isfahan, Fars, Kerman, Qazvin and the western lands, all of Persia held by the Hotaks

ledger.note: November 1729: Persia is lost to Nader. 'After 1729, Hotak rule was limited to the south of Afghanistan, and Nader Shah drove out the remaining Ghilji forces from Persia'; Ashraf was killed near the Sistan border in early 1730. Nader acted for Tahmasp II (Safavid), whose forces had taken Mashhad in November 1726.

region.text: the part of the 1727 outline that the Safavid 1721 outline does not reach: east Kerman and Yazd, South and Razavi Khorasan, Herat, Farah, Badghis, Ghor, Faryab, Sari Pul, Jawzjan and Mary

ledger.note: November 1729: the rest of the 1727 outline is lost with the Persian lands. The loss above names safavid-dynasty, and the compiler applies it as that dossier's matching gain (safavid-dynasty ledger[66], 1729-10), whose region is the Safavid 1721 outline inside the 1727 shape: 3,888 of the 5,243 cells. The other 1,359 cells would have stayed Hotak until the 1730 keyframe. Hotak dynasty page: '1729: Ashraf Hotak was banished to what is now southern Afghanistan, limiting Hotak rule to a vestige of their once large empire', and 'the southern areas of Afghanistan remained under their control until 1738'. The page names no taker for these lands, so the counterpart is nobody.

region.text: Kandahar and the Hotak lands of Hussain

ledger.note: 24 March 1738: Nader Shah takes Kandahar. Infobox 'Dissolved: 1738', 'Siege of Kandahar: 24 March 1738' (the Hussain page: reign to 25 March 1738); 'Nader Shah's forces went on to conquer Kandahar in 1738', 'besieged and destroyed' the last Hotak seat; Hussain was deported to Mazandaran.

March 1738: the Hotak dynasty ends. Hussain Hotak 'was defeated by Nader Shah in 1738 and subsequently deported to Mazandaran'; the Hussain page: the capture was 'only a temporary interruption before the founding of the last Afghan Empire in 1747' (the Durrani Empire).

wars.name: Hotak revolt against the Safavids
wars.outcome: The Hotaks keep Kandahar: Gurgin Khan (George XI) killed on 21 April 1709, the Persian armies of 1710 and the next 18 months defeated, the commander of 1712 dead at Herat.

wars.name: Hotaki invasion of Persia
wars.outcome: Kerman besieged from 1720, its town (not the citadel) conquered in October 1721 and the city not captured by 1722; the Persian army routed at Gulnabad on 8 March 1722; Isfahan falls on 23 October 1722; Shiraz, Golpayegan and Kashan follow.

wars.name: Ottoman-Hotaki war
wars.outcome: The Afghans won at Khorramabad (November 1726); the agreement of October 1727, not ratified, let the Ottomans keep the Iranian lands they occupied and recognised Ashraf.
wars.note: Russia: Ashraf lost a battle near Langarud in 1727 and signed a treaty at Rasht in February 1729; the pages name no territory.

wars.name: Nader's reconquest of Persia
wars.outcome: Nader beat Ashraf at Mehmandust (29 September 1729) and entered Isfahan on 16 November; Zarghan and Pol-e Fasa broke the Afghan army; Ashraf was killed in early 1730.

wars.name: Siege of Kandahar (1738)
wars.outcome: Nader Shah's forces took Kandahar on 24 March 1738 (infobox of the Hotak page); Hussain Hotak was deported to Mazandaran.
wars.note: The Hussain page gives no start date for the siege; the years 1736-1737 are not on any page opened.

certainty.note: The Kandahar core is a city and its province; the Persian conquests are held as cities (Kerman, Isfahan, Shiraz, Kashan) and their hinterlands, and the western edge with the Ottomans is not described.

sources.title: Hotak dynasty
sources.note: Infobox (revolt 21 April 1709, siege of Kandahar 24 March 1738, capitals, rulers, no area), Kerman 1720, Gulnabad and Isfahan 1722, Damghan 1729, Kandahar 1738.

sources.title: Mahmud Hotak
sources.note: 1717 accession, Kerman 1720-1721, Gulnabad 8 March 1722, Isfahan 23 October 1722, Shiraz, Golpayegan and Kashan, Qazvin revolt January 1723, death 22 April 1725.

sources.title: Ashraf Hotak
sources.note: Accession 1725, the Ottoman war 1726-1727, Russian treaty of Rasht 1729, Mehmandust 29 September 1729, flight from Isfahan 13 November 1729, death in early 1730.

sources.title: Mirwais Hotak
sources.note: Revolt of 1709, Persian armies of 1710, death November 1715. Silent on the territory held and on Baluchistan.

sources.title: Hussain Hotak
sources.note: Kandahar under Hussain until 1738, deported to Mazandaran, 'temporary interruption' before 1747. Silent on other territory and on the siege dates.

notes:
Cliopatria row reviewed: Hotaki Dynasty (1709-1737, 6 shapes) plus three new keyframes (1722, 1730, 1738). The row ends in 1737; the dynasty falls on 24 March 1738, so the dossier runs to 1738 (month 3) with a one-year keyframe.

Disagreements and silences: (1) the shapes of 1721-1726 lack Isfahan, which Cliopatria first draws in 1727 although the pages give Isfahan (23 October 1722), Shiraz, Golpayegan and Kashan (1722-1723); (2) Cliopatria keeps the Persian lands to 1733, but all pages put the loss in 1729-1730 (Isfahan 13 November 1729, Ashraf killed early 1730); (3) the 1718 growth (Sistan, Balochistan, Makran) and the Sistan-Balochistan part of the 1734-1737 shape are on no page opened (the Mirwais page is silent on Quetta and Baluchistan; the Hussain page names only Kandahar); (4) Herat: Mahmud beat the Sadozai Sultanate of Herat in 1720 but no page has Herat held, and Cliopatria's 37.5 N north edge is unexplained; (5) Qazvin, Yazd, Hamadan and the Caucasus: Qazvin taken and lost in January 1723, Yazd not taken, the Ottomans and Russians took land 'during the chaos' (undated), and the 'Treaty of Hamadan' is not on the Ashraf page (an unratified agreement of October 1727), so the west edge of the 1727 shape is the researcher's best outline, soft; (6) Ashraf's reign 1725-1729 (table) or 1730 (infobox); Hussain from 1725 (infobox, as King of Kandahar) or 1729; (7) Mehmandust: 29 September 1729 on the Ashraf page, the infobox of the Hotak page gives Damghan on the same date (the body: October 1729).

Counterparts: the Persian side is recorded under safavid-dynasty (Mahmud against Shah Soltan Hoseyn 1722; Tahmasp II and Nader 1729), which Cliopatria keeps to 1737; Nader's own regime is afsharid-iran from 1734. The matching losses should be in the safavid-dynasty (me-10) and afsharid-iran dossiers; the ottoman-empire and russian-empire dossiers should open the pages for 1723-1727. The kingdom of Kartli (George XI, killed 1709) is a Cliopatria row (kingdom-of-kartli, 1463-1705); not a counterpart here.

Area: no infobox area on the Hotak page, so no ratio. Page that would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Kandahar_(1738) (url_not_found, retried once); the siege rests on the Hotak page infobox (24 March 1738) and the Hussain page, with no start date. Pages: five opened (the budget).

FIX fx-14 2026-11-01 (F057, snap at 1734: 6,661 ledger cells against 2,114 in the keyframe). Cause: hotaki-dynasty_1727 and _1721 had no from/to, so data/shapes.csv kept them alive to 1733 and 1726; the compiler draws the union of all keyframes alive in a year, so 1730-1733 held the 1727 outline again (3,854 cells added at 1730) until the 1734 keyframe dropped it. Now 1727 runs 1727-1729 and 1721 only 1721. A second loss (1729-11, counterpart nobody) removes the 1,359 cells of the 1727 outline outside the Safavid mirror gain. Page: Hotak dynasty.

F074 (fx-14, conflict with khanate-of-kalat 1718-1738, 661 cells a year in Baluchistan and Sistan and Baluchestan): kept, nothing changed. The Hotak dynasty page (opened 2026-11-01) is silent on Balochistan, Makran, Quetta and Kalat; it has the Hotaks 'cross the deserts of Sistan' to Kerman in 1720 and nothing more. The Khanate of Kalat page has Abdullah Khan (1716-1731) extend the state 'to Persia till the port of Bandar Abbas'. The size rule gives the cells to the khanate; the Hotak claim to them rests on Cliopatria's outline alone. Fix fx-49 (2 Nov 2026): the ledger gain of the Kerman province (October 1721, former ledger/7) is deleted, ledger 8 onward move up by one; the Mahmud Hotak page has the town conquered but the citadel not taken and, in 1722, 'failed to capture it' (R088).
